examples.subject: 高山湖泊
examples.author: Adrien Olichon
examples.first_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE standalone finished art print from IMAGE 1, the content photograph. IMAGE 2 is a composite reference: use ONLY ITS LOWER ARTWORK HALF as a style/material reference, not its upper photograph or its subject. Match its restrained handmade print language, broad warm ivory uncoated paper, restrained ink and abundant negative space. Output a portrait art print, approximately 2:3. Place the simplified artwork in the lower-middle area, with about 55–65% paper left blank overall. Do not render an original-photo panel, comparison grid, frame, mat, border, title, lettering, numbers, signature, logo, watermark or geography. Empty paper instead of text. Do not introduce actual new objects or decorative sun/circles. Preserve the specific subject and relations of image 1 while simplifying texture. No photorealistic patches, smooth gradients, glossy 3D paper, drop shadows, vector-perfect outlines or cartoon look.
Content invariants: Preserve this specific broad rocky mountainside descending from upper left to right, the continuous lake shoreline below and the pale lake foreground. The mountain is a ridge, not a single pointed pyramid. Preserve the relative ridge profile. Remove microscopic rock detail and clouds.
Style: Minimal torn-paper collage with dry-brush, flat color planes and fibrous deckled edges. Use dark charcoal and gray torn planes with muted olive slopes; a short pale sage dry-brush lake band below, and one small pale blue sky scrap. Interpret the ridge as 5–7 broad planes, not a detailed etching.
